claim: The Reproducibility Project: Cancer Biology seeks to address growing concerns about reproducibility in scientific research by conducting replications of selected experiments from a number of high-profile papers in the field of cancer biology.
source: The Reproducibility Project: Cancer Biology seeks to address growing concerns about reproducibility in scientific research by conducting replications of selected experiments from a number of high-profile papers in the field of cancer biology.
evidence: This is stated as the purpose of the Reproducibility Project in the abstract.

claim: The papers selected for replication were published between 2010 and 2012.
source: The papers, which were published between 2010 and 2012, were selected on the basis of citations and Altmetric scores (Errington et al., 2014).

claim: Papers were selected on the basis of citations and Altmetric scores.
source: The papers, which were published between 2010 and 2012, were selected on the basis of citations and Altmetric scores (Errington et al., 2014).
evidence: Supported by citation to Errington et al., 2014.

claim: This Registered Report describes the proposed replication plan of key experiments from 'COT drives resistance to RAF inhibition through MAPK pathway reactivation' by Johannessen and colleagues, published in Nature in 2010.
source: This Registered Report describes the proposed replication plan of key experiments from "COT drives resistance to RAF inhibition through MAPK pathway reactivation" by Johannessen and colleagues, published in Nature in 2010 (Johannessen et al., 2010).

claim: The key experiments to be replicated are those reported in Figures 3B, 3D-E, 3I, and 4E-F.
source: The key experiments to be replicated are those reported in Figures 3B, 3D-E, 3I, and 4E-F.
evidence: Direct statement of which figures will be replicated.

claim: RPMI-7951 and OUMS023 cells exhibit robust ERK/MEK activity concomitant with reduced growth sensitivity in the presence of the BRAF inhibitor PLX4720.
source: In Figures 3B, D-E, RPMI-7951 and OUMS023 cells were reported to exhibit robust ERK/MEK activity concomitant with reduced growth sensitivity in the presence of the BRAF inhibitor PLX4720.
evidence: Reported findings from the original study being replicated.

claim: MAP3K8 (COT/TPL2) directly regulates MEK/ERK phosphorylation.
source: MAP3K8 (COT/TPL2) directly regulated MEK/ERK phosphorylation, as the treatment of RPMI-7951 cells with a MAP3K8 kinase inhibitor resulted in a dose-dependent suppression of MEK/ERK activity (Figure 3I).
evidence: Supported by experimental data showing dose-dependent suppression.

claim: Treatment of RPMI-7951 cells with a MAP3K8 kinase inhibitor results in a dose-dependent suppression of MEK/ERK activity.
source: MAP3K8 (COT/TPL2) directly regulated MEK/ERK phosphorylation, as the treatment of RPMI-7951 cells with a MAP3K8 kinase inhibitor resulted in a dose-dependent suppression of MEK/ERK activity (Figure 3I).

claim: MAP3K8-deficient A375 cells remain sensitive to BRAF inhibition, exhibiting reduced growth and MEK/ERK activity during inhibitor treatment.
source: In contrast, MAP3K8-deficient A375 cells remained sensitive to BRAF inhibition, exhibiting reduced growth and MEK/ERK activity during inhibitor treatment.
evidence: Reported experimental observation from original study.

claim: MAP3K8-expressing A375 cells treated with PLX4720 along with MEK inhibitors significantly inhibit both cell viability and ERK activation compared to treatment with PLX4720 alone.
source: To determine if RAF and MEK inhibitors together can overcome single-agent resistance, MAP3K8-expressing A375 cells treated with PLX4720 along with MEK inhibitors significantly inhibited both cell viability and ERK activation compared to treatment with PLX4720 alone, as reported in Figures 4E-F.

claim: Activation of the canonical mitogen activated protein kinase (MAPK) pathway occurs in response to the binding of growth factors, hormones, or neurotransmitters to receptor tyrosine kinase receptors located at the cell surface.
source: Activation of the canonical mitogen activated protein kinase (MAPK) pathway occurs in response to the binding of growth factors, hormones, or neurotransmitters to receptor tyrosine kinase receptors located at the cell surface (Dhomen and Marais, 2009; Lopez-Bergami et al., 2008).
evidence: Supported by citations to established literature.

claim: In untransformed cells, receptor ligation induces the sequential activation of RAS, RAF, MEK and ERK, which relays proliferative signals from the cell periphery into the nucleus to control cellular survival, differentiation and growth.
source: In untransformed cells, receptor ligation induces the sequential activation of the small GTPase RAS, followed by RAF, MEK and ERK, which relays proliferative signals generated at the cell periphery into the nucleus to control cellular survival, differentiation and growth (Inamdar et al., 2010; Panka et al., 2006).
evidence: Supported by citations to established literature.

claim: Dysregulation of MAPK signaling is common in many human cancers including melanoma.
source: Not surprisingly, dysregulation of MAPK signaling is common in many human cancers including melanoma.
evidence: General statement about cancer biology supported by context and citations.

claim: Mutations in the RAF and RAS genes that trigger constitutive activation of the MAPK pathway can result in uncontrolled cell proliferation, invasion, metastasis, survival and angiogenesis.
source: Mutations in the RAF and RAS genes (Davies et al., 2002; Mercer and Pritchard, 2003) that trigger constitutive activation of the MAPK pathway can result in uncontrolled cell proliferation, invasion, metastasis, survival and angiogenesis (Panka et al., 2006; Sharma et al., 2006; Smalley et al., 2006; Smalley and Herlyn, 2006).

claim: BRAF is one of three members of the RAF family, which includes ARAF, BRAF, and CRAF (or RAF-1).
source: BRAF is one of three members of the RAF family, which includes ARAF, BRAF, and CRAF (or RAF-1) (Dhomen and Marais, 2009).

claim: In melanoma, BRAF represents the most commonly mutated gene in the MAPK signaling cascade.
source: In melanoma, BRAF represents the most commonly mutated gene in the MAPK signaling cascade where 90% of tumors carry a valine to glutamic acid transition at codon 600 (V600E) that renders BRAF constitutively active and hyperactivates the MAPK cascade (Davies et al., 2002; Dhomen and Marais, 2009; Michaloglou et al., 2008).

claim: 90% of melanoma tumors carry a valine to glutamic acid transition at codon 600 (V600E) that renders BRAF constitutively active and hyperactivates the MAPK cascade.
source: In melanoma, BRAF represents the most commonly mutated gene in the MAPK signaling cascade where 90% of tumors carry a valine to glutamic acid transition at codon 600 (V600E) that renders BRAF constitutively active and hyperactivates the MAPK cascade (Davies et al., 2002; Dhomen and Marais, 2009; Michaloglou et al., 2008).

claim: Targeting BRAF (V600E) melanomas with RAF-selective inhibitors results in initial tumor regression.
source: While preclinical and clinical studies have shown that targeting BRAF (V600E) melanomas with the use of RAF-selective inhibitors results in initial tumor regression (Fedorenko et al., 2015; Flaherty et al., 2010; Shtivelman et al., 2014), responses to RAF inhibitors are transient, with acquired resistance triggering disease progression (Shtivelman et al., 2014).
evidence: Supported by citations to preclinical and clinical studies.

claim: Responses to RAF inhibitors are transient, with acquired resistance triggering disease progression.
source: While preclinical and clinical studies have shown that targeting BRAF (V600E) melanomas with the use of RAF-selective inhibitors results in initial tumor regression (Fedorenko et al., 2015; Flaherty et al., 2010; Shtivelman et al., 2014), responses to RAF inhibitors are transient, with acquired resistance triggering disease progression (Shtivelman et al., 2014).

claim: RPMI-7951 and OUMS-23 cells express high intrinsic levels of MAP3K8 compared to A375 cells where MAP3K8 is undetectable.
source: As shown in Figure 3B and reported by others, RPMI-7951 and OUMS-23 cells were found to express high intrinsic levels of MAP3K8 compared to A375 cells where MAP3K8 was undetectable (Johannessen et al., 2010; Paraiso et al., 2012).
evidence: Supported by Figure 3B and multiple citations.

claim: RPMI-7981 cells treated with PLX4032/vemurafenib remain refractory to inhibitor treatment as assessed by annexin V staining.
source: This is supported by additional findings demonstrating that RPMI-7981 cells treated with the closely related BRAF inhibitor PLX4032/vemurafenib (a successor of PLX4720) also remain refractory to inhibitor treatment as assessed by annexin V staining (Paraiso et al., 2012) and MTS assay (Park et al., 2013).
evidence: Supported by citation to Paraiso et al., 2012.

claim: RPMI-7981 cells treated with PLX4032/vemurafenib remain refractory to inhibitor treatment as assessed by MTS assay.
source: This is supported by additional findings demonstrating that RPMI-7981 cells treated with the closely related BRAF inhibitor PLX4032/vemurafenib (a successor of PLX4720) also remain refractory to inhibitor treatment as assessed by annexin V staining (Paraiso et al., 2012) and MTS assay (Park et al., 2013).
evidence: Supported by citation to Park et al., 2013.

claim: Some studies have reported RPMI-7981 cells as exhibiting modest sensitivity to PLX4720.
source: However, others have reported RPMI-7981 cells as exhibiting modest sensitivity to PLX4720 (Schayowitz et al., 2012).
evidence: Supported by citation to Schayowitz et al., 2012.

claim: ERK activity was reduced by 50% after incubation with PLX4720 inhibitor in RPMI-7981 cells.
source: In the latter case, ERK activity was reduced by 50% after incubation with inhibitor, although these differences in sensitivity may reflect the significantly shorter time course and experimental design used by Park and colleagues.
evidence: Reported observation with inference about experimental differences.

claim: MAP3K8 kinase activity is required to regulate MEK/ERK activation in RPMI-7951 cells.
source: Finally, in Figure 3I, Johannessen and colleagues determined that MAP3K8 kinase activity is required to regulate MEK/ERK activation in RPMI-7951 cells, findings that further confirm MAP3K8 is an essential upstream activator of the MEK-ERK signaling cascade (George and Salmeron, 2009; Johannessen et al., 2010).

claim: MAP3K8 is an essential upstream activator of the MEK-ERK signaling cascade.
source: Finally, in Figure 3I, Johannessen and colleagues determined that MAP3K8 kinase activity is required to regulate MEK/ERK activation in RPMI-7951 cells, findings that further confirm MAP3K8 is an essential upstream activator of the MEK-ERK signaling cascade (George and Salmeron, 2009; Johannessen et al., 2010).

claim: Resistance to targeted agents, such as BRAF inhibitors, is a frequent cause of therapy failure.
source: Resistance to targeted agents, such as BRAF inhibitors, is a frequent cause of therapy failure, as noted above.
evidence: General statement supported by prior discussion and citations.

claim: Chronic BRAF inhibition can lead to cross-resistance to several BRAF-selective inhibitors.
source: Importantly, chronic BRAF inhibition can lead to cross-resistance to several BRAF-selective inhibitors, indicating that resistance is not likely to be overcome by switching to a new RAF inhibitor (Corcoran et al., 2010; Villanueva et al., 2011).

claim: Resistance to BRAF inhibitors is not likely to be overcome by switching to a new RAF inhibitor.
source: Importantly, chronic BRAF inhibition can lead to cross-resistance to several BRAF-selective inhibitors, indicating that resistance is not likely to be overcome by switching to a new RAF inhibitor (Corcoran et al., 2010; Villanueva et al., 2011).

claim: Combination treatment with MEK and BRAF inhibitors may be useful in preventing the emergence of resistance or in overcoming resistance to single agent therapies.
source: It has been suggested previously that combination treatment with MEK and BRAF inhibitors may be useful in preventing the emergence of resistance or in overcoming resistance to single agent therapies targeting either molecule alone (Corcoran et al., 2010).

claim: Both viability and ERK activation were dramatically reduced in MAP3K8-expressing A375 cells treated with combination therapies of PLX4720 with either CI-1040 or AZD6244.
source: As shown in Figures 4E and 4F, both viability and ERK activation was dramatically reduced in MAP3K8-expressing cells treated with either of the combination therapies, similar to cells ectopically expressing MEK1, which remained sensitive to PLX4720 (Johannessen et al., 2010).
evidence: Supported by Figures 4E and 4F and citation.

claim: A375 cells ectopically expressing MEK1 remained sensitive to PLX4720.
source: As shown in Figures 4E and 4F, both viability and ERK activation was dramatically reduced in MAP3K8-expressing cells treated with either of the combination therapies, similar to cells ectopically expressing MEK1, which remained sensitive to PLX4720 (Johannessen et al., 2010).
evidence: Supported by Figures 4E and 4F and citation.

claim: Similar results were obtained in RPMI-7951 cells expressing high basal levels of MAP3K8 treated with PLX4032 and MEK inhibitor AS703026.
source: Similar results were obtained in RPMI-7951 cells expressing high basal levels of MAP3K8 treated with PLX4032 and a second MEK inhibitor AS703026 (Park et al., 2013).
evidence: Supported by citation to Park et al., 2013.

claim: Overexpression of constitutively active MEK (MEK1DD) resulted in increased sensitivity to BRAF inhibition combined with AZD6244, but not CI-1040.
source: Interestingly, overexpression of constitutively active MEK (MEK1DD) resulted in increased sensitivity to BRAF inhibition combined with AZD6244, but not CI-1040 (Johannessen et al., 2010).

claim: MAP3K8 is able to reactivate MAPK signaling despite BRAF inhibition.
source: These findings confirm that MAP3K8 is able to reactivate MAPK signaling despite BRAF inhibition and that targeting RAF and MEK in combination may be an effective anti-melanoma treatment strategy.

claim: Targeting RAF and MEK in combination may be an effective anti-melanoma treatment strategy.
source: These findings confirm that MAP3K8 is able to reactivate MAPK signaling despite BRAF inhibition and that targeting RAF and MEK in combination may be an effective anti-melanoma treatment strategy.
evidence: Inference from experimental findings with speculative element.
